dedupe_keys.name: accessmod 5 physical accessibility to health care

description: AccessMod 5 is free, open-source software that models how physically accessible health services are to a population. It computes travel time surfaces to the nearest facility using anisotropic, multimodal movement over land cover, roads and barriers; estimates the part of the population not served when facilities lack capacity; measures referral times and distances between facilities; summarises coverage by administrative area; and finds the best locations for new facilities in a scaling-up analysis. The provider is the World Health Organization, with the GeoHealth group of the University of Geneva, which develops it with the MORU Health GeoLab; UNICEF supported maintenance from 2018 to 2021, and it has been a Digital Public Good since 2022. It applies worldwide wherever users supply national land cover, road, facility and population data. The code is on GitHub under the GNU GPL version 3, with an additional WHO terms of use and software licence agreement, and runs in Docker or a VirtualBox virtual machine with a browser interface built on GRASS, GDAL, R and Shiny. A companion R package, inAccessMod, automates downloading and preparing the input layers (administrative boundaries, elevation, population, land cover and OpenStreetMap roads and barriers) and processing WHO HeRAMS facility tables. Caveats: results depend on assumed travel speeds and input data quality, and seasonal flooding or disruption must be modelled as separate scenarios. Simulation uses: service coverage when roads or facilities are disrupted by floods or conflict, emergency referral planning, and facility siting. Related records: the Malaria Atlas Project travel time maps (data-map-travel-time-to-healthcare) provide a global precomputed equivalent.
